title: Finite-Tor constructibility of the evaluated unit
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and positive quotients $A_{n+1}=R/\varpi^{n+1}$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $W$, use strict semilinear coefficient systems and their ordinary derived category and exact evaluations [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus, def-coef-finite-adjunction-system-data]. For every scheme $W$ and every $n\in\mathbf N$, the nth derived evaluation of its actual coefficient unit [def-sf-finite-adjunction-coefficient-unit] belongs to the finite-Tor constructible domain [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. No geometric finiteness of W is assumed.

proof.text: Exact evaluation commutes with the derived degree-zero single functor. The evaluated regular module is the regular finite coefficient sheaf, by the identity on sections. It is locally constant free of rank one; on the one-stratum decomposition of W it therefore has finite stalks and is constructible. Its cohomology is concentrated in degree zero and tensoring with it is the identity. Thus its Tor interval is [0,0], including when W is empty.
